 JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.4342/2020 That on 07.09.2019 at about 9.20 p.m., when the Petitioner was proceeding in his Maruthi Omni Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-NE-6319 to Hosakote to sell the flowers grown in his land and when he reached near Baluvahalli gate at Vijipura - Channarayapatna Road via Vijipura to Devanahalli, at that time, one Ashok Leyland School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-43- 1896 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and at high speed and dashed against the Petitioner's car and caused the accident.
Due to which, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries to his whole body.
3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to MTB Hospital and after first aid treatment he was shifted to Suguna hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

The Petitioner had spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
4.

Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was an Agriculturist and doing flower SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4342/2020 business and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month from both source.
Due to the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, he could not do his work and he lost income from the date of accident.
The accidental injuries have caused permanent disability to the Petitioner.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Ashok Leyland School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-43-1896 by its driver.

The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Ashok Leyland School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-43- 1896 and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection statements to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4342/2020 accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the Mariswamy vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172261953/

Further it contended that the entire negligence is on the part of the Petitioner who has driven his Omni car in a rash and negligently and directly hit to the front right portion of the bus.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it contended that offending vehicle was insured with SCCH 15 6 MVC No.4342/2020 the Respondent No.1 and the policy was valid at the time of the accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Ashok Leyland School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-43-1896 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
3) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for  compensation?
If so, how much and from  whom?

It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Ashok Leyland School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-43-1896 by its driver.
10. On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 and 2 had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Ashok Leyland School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 43-1896 by its driver.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 15 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and 18 & 19 and he has re-iterated the Petition averments in his Chief-affidavit.

Ex.P.1 to 13 and 18 & 19 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Charge sheet, Spot Mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate, Discharge summary, SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4342/2020 Rent Agreement, Pharmacy list, Medical bills, Final bill, School Certificate and Books.

PW.2 has reiterated the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in RTA.
PW.3 deposed that he was the driver of the Omni Car wherein the Petitioner has travelled on the date of accident.
14. P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1.

It is the main contention of the Respondent No.1 that on the alleged date of accident, the Petitioner himself was the driver of the Omini SCCH 15 11 MVC No.4342/2020 Car and he himself caused the accident.

During the stage of Arguments, the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 also vehemently argued that on the alleged date of accident the Petitioner was the driver and he caused the accident and PW.1 admitted the same in his cross-examination.
15. Upon going through the cross-examination of PW.1, he deposed that on the alleged date of accident he himself had driven the said car and he is the owner of the car.
Further he stated that he has not given any statement before the police about the accident.
Further he stated that he does not know Prabhakar S/o Venkateshappa and he does not know after investigation the police have filed Charge-sheet against the Prabhakar S/o Venkateshappa.
16. The Petitioner has examined Prabhakar S/o Venkateshappa as PW.3.

PW.3 has deposed that on the alleged date of accident, he himself and Petitioner were going to Hoskote market to sell Rose flowers and he was driving the car and then the offending bus came with rash and negligently SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4342/2020 and dashed against the Omni car.
He also got some injuries and the Petitioner also sustained injuries.
Further he deposed that he does not know who is the owner of the said Omini Car which he has driven on the alleged date of accident.

Further he deposed that he has not given statement before the police and he does not know against him the police have filed Charge- sheet and he does not know about Murali Mohan and he does not know that the Complaint was lodged against him.
It is to be noted here that PW.3 deposed in the cross-examination that on the alleged date, the bus dashed to his side where he sat in the car.
But, he sustained simple injury.
It is to be observed here that the Petitioner got grievous injuries in the said accident.
If PW.3 had sustained simple injuries, certainly he was concious after the accident.
But, in the cross-examination he stated that he does not know who has taken them to the hospital and he does not know the name of the hospital.
So, the evidence of PW.3 does not inspire the confidence of the Court and his testimony is not believable.
Added to it, the evidence of PW.1 is very clear that he himself has driven the Omni car on the alleged date of accident.

Though, the Charge-sheet was filed against the PW.3 alleging that PW.3 had driven the said vehicle on the date of accident, the evidence of PW.1 itself shows that he drove the said Maruthi car at the time accident.
The Spot Sketch and Spot mahazar shows that the alleged accident was occurred on the middle of the road.
Further Ex.P5 i.e., IMV report shows that front portion of both vehicles got damaged.

Hence, this tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has contributed 50% of negligence towards the accident and the driver of the offending vehicle Mariswamy vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172261953/

18. Issue No.2 & 3:
Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.

SCCH 15 14 MVC No.4342/2020 As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Ashok Leyland School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-43-1896 by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
19. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 55 years.
Further, in the School Certificate i.e., Ex.P-18, date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 15.08.1965.
The accident has taken place on 07.09.2019.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the Petitioner was 54 years and 22 days.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner to be taken at 55 years for the purpose of assessement of compensation.
20 . Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was working as an Agriculturist and doing Flower business and was earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has produced Passbook for the sale of flowers at Ex.P19.
Upon going through the said document, it does not reflects what is profit.
Further in the cross-examination he admitted that said Ex.P19 shows that it started from 17.01.2019 to 28.11.2019.
SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4342/2020 He also admitted that he could not get the entire amount mentioned in the said documents.
Further he admitted that he has not produced any document to show that after deducting expenses what is his profit.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that,
it is proper to take Rs.14,000/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
21.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS
PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING
The Petitioner has deposed that he had sustained grievous injuries.

The Wound Certificate i.e.,
Ex.P-6 issued by the Medical Officer of the Suguna Hospital, Bengaluru, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injury i.e., SCCH 15 16 MVC No.4342/2020 1) Blunt injury to abdomen - Haemoperitonem with hollow viscous perforation gangrenous SI 2) Depressed fracture right lateral condyle Tibia
As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injuries are grievous in nature.
23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.75,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
24. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.4342/2020 III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
25. The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he has taken treatment as an inpatient at Suguna hospital, Bengaluru.
Ex.P.8 & 10 are the Discharge summaries of the Petitioner relating to the Suguna Hospital, Bengaluru.
It shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 07.09.2019 to 18.09.2019.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 12 days.
26. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/- under this head (@ Rs.14,000/- per month ).
 SCCH 15 18 MVC No.4342/2020  IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
27.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- (@ Rs.100/- per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
28. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced Medical bills and hospital bills and Final bill, which is marked at SCCH 15 19 MVC No.4342/2020 Ex.P.12 & 13.
I have gone through the same and the acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.4,72,320/-.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,72,320/- under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS /
COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:

sentences.text: The Petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

30. Further the Petitioner got examined the doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by the Petitioner.
Further, he has assessed the Permanent disability of the Petitioner towards right lower Limb at 40% and whole body disability at 13%.
Further, PW.2 got marked Case sheet, Clinical notes and X-ray SCCH 15 20 MVC No.4342/2020 at Ex.P14 to 16.
In the cross-examination of PW.2 he deposed that he has treated the Petitioner and he suggested the Petitioner to take Physiotherapy treatment for two months.
But, he has not seen the Physiotherapy treatment documents.
Further he admitted that the Petitioner has not taken any further treatment.
Further he stated that he does not know the avocation of the Petitioner.
Now, at present the Petitioner does not have any problem to abdomen.
Further he admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner is united.
Further he also admitted that he has not given any estimation for the removal of implants.

Hence, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the evidence of PW.2 and the documents marked, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
31. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 11.

With multiplier of 11, income of Rs.14,000/- per month and disability of the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.4342/2020 Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to 1,47,840/- (Rs.14,000/- x 12 = 1,68,000/-, Rs.1,68,000/-x 11 x 8/100 = 1,47,840/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,47,840/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
32.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 75,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-
3. Loss of income during the Rs. 28,000/-
laid up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/- diet, and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses Rs.4,72,320/-
6. Loss of Future Income Rs.1,47,840/-

Total Rs.7,71,160/-

sentences.text: 8 33. Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.7,71,160/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
34. Regarding Liability:

This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Ashok Leyland School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-43-1896 and by the Petitioner.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, this tribunal comes to conclusion that the driver of offending bus has contributed 50% of negligence towards the accident and the Petitioner has contributed 50% of negligence towards the accident.
Therefore, the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount out of the total compensation to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.2, has to pay the compensation amount to the SCCH 15 23 MVC No.4342/2020 Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 are "Partly in the Affirmative".
35. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.7,71,160/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 jointly and  severally are liable to pay 50% of the  compensation amount out of the total  compensation amount awarded to the  Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and SCCH 15 24 MVC No.4342/2020 interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.

ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.7,71,160/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 jointly and  severally are liable to pay 50% of the  compensation amount out of the total  compensation amount awarded to the  Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and SCCH 15 24 MVC No.4342/2020 interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
